Senses.Explanation: To continue the lineage lamps is to carry Chan succession from predecessor to successor and from generation to generation. Yongjue Yuanxian defines the governing lamp image in the Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian: successive transmission is compared to a lamp because it breaks darkness and reveals things, and because its illumination can continue without end. His histories then call more than seventy generations an unbroken chain of linked lamps and describe them as linking the lamps while continuing the flame. Hanxiu Ruqian uses the phrase in memorial verses for succession after receiving his predecessor's blows and for two named lineage holders carrying the line in different regions. Zefeng Yue applies it to an ancestral portrait during a teaching-seat address. These uses concern public lineage continuity, not ordinary lamps physically fastened together.
Senses.Note: The exact headword has 104 occurrences in 28 allowed texts. Most belong to the book title treated in the second sense; the free phrase recurs with being unbroken, continuing the flame, succession, generations, ancestral portraits, and separate teaching regions. A complete concordance review found no independently attested hardware sense. A festival line about lamps and the moon reverses the graph order and therefore does not establish one.

Occurrences.Kwic: 自興聖肇基，聯燈不絕，七十餘代，禪化大行。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄), in Yongjue Yuanxian's own Drum Mountain history, says that from Xingsheng's foundation the linked lamps remained unbroken for more than seventy generations. The whole prose unit is historical composition, not an embedded quotation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 厥後聯燈續焰者七十餘代，可謂罕匹其休者也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄), in another first-person Drum Mountain composition by Yongjue Yuanxian, describes more than seventy generations as linking the lamps and continuing the flame.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曾遭痛棒送頭顱，續燄聯燈道不孤，恩大難酬無著處，栴檀一瓣爇枯株。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hanxiu (憨休禪師語錄), in Hanxiu Ruqian's memorial act for his late teacher Yun, explicitly marks Hanxiu as the incense speaker. Hanxiu says that after receiving painful blows he continues the flame and links the lamp so the Way is not alone.

Occurrences.Kwic: 昔年聚首在鮦陽，其後聯燈各一方，君自中州行祖令，我從關內整頹綱。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hanxiu (憨休禪師語錄), in Hanxiu Ruqian's memorial for Chonghan Heshang, states that Hanxiu prepared the memorial and spoke. Hanxiu recalls that the two later linked lamps in separate regions, one carrying the ancestral command in the central provinces and the other restoring the community order within the passes.

Occurrences.Kwic: 遂插香曰：一㡧次第聯燈遠，四面好山潑黛青。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, fascicles 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), in the explicitly headed section for Zefeng Yue of Jubao in Dingzhou, records Zefeng Yue establishing the patriarchs' room, mounting the teaching seat, inserting incense, and speaking of one portrait linking the lamp far away in succession.

Senses.Explanation: The book Linked-Lamp Essentials is a specific Chan compilation, not the act of continuing a lineage. In his self-preface, Huiweng Wuming says that he selected material from more than six hundred teachers, arranged encounters, questions and answers, comments on old and recent cases, and essential statements under each person's chapter, divided the work into thirty fascicles, and gave it this title. Li Yong's preface says the title was placed on the work and the blocks were carved for circulation. Yongjue Yuanxian later places Wuming's compilation among the five lamp records. A lineage biography records Wuming as its compiler, while Sichong's republication preface calls it the Linked-Lamp Record and recounts its printing history.
Senses.Note: This is a different thing from lineage succession: it is a named thirty-fascicle text with a compiler, contents, prefaces, printing blocks, circulation history, and an abbreviated record title. The full title occurs 77 times in 13 allowed texts; the shorter title occurs once. The explicit referent label in the preferred target keeps the distinction visible without relying on capitalization alone.

Occurrences.Kwic: 提唱機緣，問答語句，拈提古今，得其要妙者，各逐本人章次收錄，離為三十卷，命曰聯燈會要。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linked-Lamp Essentials (聯燈會要), Huiweng Wuming's signed self-preface: Huiweng inventories the selected encounter material, says it was divided into thirty fascicles, and directly gives the work its title.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (聯燈會要). Li Yong is the named preface author.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The title clause occurs in Li Yong’s named preface; Li Yong states that the work was titled Linked-Lamp Essentials and carved for circulation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 迄淳熈間晦翁明公作聯燈會要，其同時復有雷菴受公亦謂其所收未詳，復作普燈以廣之
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄), Yongjue's own preface: Yongjue directly reports that Huiweng Wuming made Linked-Lamp Essentials during the Chunxi era.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師纂修聯燈會要，傳于叢林。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (增集續傳燈錄). Compiler narration reports that Huiweng Wuming compiled the book.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The biographical clause uses 師 as its subject and the verbs 纂修 and 傳: the book-history compiler narrates that Huiweng Wuming compiled Linked-Lamp Essentials and transmitted it in the monasteries; Huiweng is the person described, not the headword utterer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 聯燈錄，乃晦翁和尚居江心潛光室時，全提機要，開鑿人天，編集聯類而成。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Linked-Lamp Essentials (聯燈會要), in the republication preface signed by the monk Sichong of Dianshan in Songjiang, uses the abbreviated title Linked-Lamp Record and says Huiweng Wuming compiled it while living in the Hidden-Light Room at Jiangxin. Sichong is the exact preface author; Wuming is the compiler described.

Occurrences.Kwic: 禪家歷世相傳，喻之為燈，取其能破暗以顯物，亦取其能繼照於無盡也。自宋景德間，道原大師始為傳燈，嗣是則有廣燈、續燈、聯燈、普燈之作
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄), in Yongjue Yuanxian's own preface to the Record of the Successive Lamp, directly defines why successive Chan transmission is compared to a lamp, then lists the lamp-record family including the Linked Lamp. The headword is a title in this row, so it supports the lineage-lamp explanation but does not buy free-phrase depth.
